title: The Rising Vent
story: Deep in the Cinder Hollow, Thrindlepyre huffs on a lava vent to flood the cavern, giggling as a family of shy stone sprites huddles on a high ledge. Mr 6 counts the glowing line creeping up the wall: 4.5 feet every hour. With a heave he cracks open three old sluice channels that carry lava away at 3 feet every hour, and the sprites need every minute he can buy them.
question: If the ledge is 9 feet above the lava right now, how many hours does Mr 6 have before the lava reaches the sprites?
solution: The channels drain lava away, so the real climb each hour is 4.5 - 3 = 1.5 feet.
The lava must climb 9 feet, so 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6.
Mr 6 has 6 hours to carry the stone sprites to safety.
praise: Setting up a rate problem was exactly right — the missing step was letting the drain channels cancel part of the lava's climb before dividing.
hint: Before you divide, ask: after one whole hour of rising AND draining, how much higher is the lava really?
victory: Mr 6 ferried every sprite up the chimney with an hour to spare, and Thrindlepyre huffed so hard at the empty ledge that he blew himself out like a birthday candle.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight in a blue cape braces open stone sluice gates in a glowing red lava cavern while a bellows-bellied fire monster puffs at a rising lava pool and tiny stone sprites cling to a high ledge.
